name: IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd
title: IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd - 532947 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Toll-road cash flows lift EBITDA 17% and PAT 51%, but no new orders won in Q1 and construction revenue fell 21%, with TOT-20/21/22 bidding pushed to late August.

triggers.label: No material new orders in Q1
triggers.quote: during the quarter, we have not bagged any orders because there was no major award activity

triggers.label: TOT-20/21/22 bidding postponed to late August
triggers.quote: the bidding has been postponed to the latter part of August

triggers.label: Toll tariff up ~2.5%, inflation 6-7%
triggers.quote: we expect higher tariff growth in the next financial year

triggers.label: Construction revenue ~₹40–43bn over two years
triggers.quote: we expect to generate approximately ₹40–43 billion in construction revenue

guidance.quote: we expect to generate approximately ₹40–43 billion in construction revenue
we expect the O&M order book to increase by around ₹4,000–₹5,000 crore every year
we expect to become net debt -free by FY2030

red_flags.label: Zero new orders in Q1; construction revenue down 21%

summary.headline: IRB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 51% to ₹306 crore on InvIT-led income growth, while construction revenue fell 21% to ₹967 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated income was flat at ₹2,173 crore (up 0.4% YoY), but mix shifted sharply toward InvIT and BOT income as construction revenue fell 21%. EBITDA rose 17% to ₹1,188 crore, lifting margins, and PAT grew 51% to ₹306 crore helped by lower interest cost and higher distributions from both InvITs. No new orders were won in the quarter, with the company citing a slow award cycle and expecting stronger second-half inflows. The TOT-20/21/22 bidding has been pushed to late August after NHAI raised upfront capex requirements.

segments.name: InvIT and related assets
segments.commentary: Income up 87% to ₹437 crore; EBITDA margin at 94%, within the company's stated 90-94% range. Private InvIT average daily toll ₹13.35 crore vs ₹9.2 crore (+45% like-for-like, excluding 3 transferred assets).

segments.name: BOT (wholly owned toll)
segments.commentary: Income up 14% to ₹733 crore; EBITDA margin around 90-91%. Mumbai-Pune toll up 9% and Ahmedabad-Vadodara up 21% YoY.

segments.name: Construction (EPC)
segments.commentary: Income down 21% to ₹967 crore on completion of projects active last year. EPC order book stands at ₹1,700 crore; ₹800-900 crore of change-of-scope works secured in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Construction revenue of ₹4,000-4,300 crore (₹40-43 billion) expected over the next two years from the existing order book, mostly O&M-linked.
Revenue mix expected to move toward roughly 50:50 construction vs O&M/InvIT over 2-3 years, with O&M at 40-50% of segment revenue.
O&M order book expected to rise ₹4,000-5,000 crore per year, depending on TOT wins.
Net debt-free by FY2030 target retained; asset base goal of ₹1,40,000 crore over 3-4 years reiterated.
Tariff revisions expected to rise in FY28 given inflation of 6-7%; FY27 tariff increase was about 2.5%.
capex_capacity: Private InvIT signed binding term sheet to transfer two BOT assets at enterprise value of ₹4,605 crore (fourth B.E.S.T. cycle); company expects ~₹2,500 crore of additional O&M contract from these assets.
Refinanced ~₹3,700 crore for wholly owned Mumbai-Pune Expressway, cutting borrowing cost ~65 bps (~₹25 crore annual saving).
Refinanced ~₹11,000 crore across six Private InvIT SPVs at Trust level (AAA), cutting borrowing cost ~160 bps (~₹180 crore annual saving).
TOT-20, TOT-21 and TOT-22 (all in Bihar): NHAI raised upfront capex; bidding postponed to late August 2026; MLFF clarifications pending.
demand_pricing: Order book ~₹44,100 crore including EPC order book of ₹1,700 crore; no major orders won in Q1 as award activity was minimal.
Government TOT/BOT pipeline of ~₹4.4 lakh crore over 4-5 years; TOT awards of ₹40,000-50,000 crore expected annually.
Average daily toll across 100% subsidiaries plus both InvITs ~₹27 crore vs ₹21.4 crore (+26% YoY).
Private InvIT distribution ~₹200 crore; IRB's 51% share ~₹102 crore vs ₹27 crore (+278%). Public InvIT distribution ~₹208 crore; IRB's ~17% share ~₹35 crore vs ₹19 crore (+84%).
BOT competition: historically 5-7 bidders; management does not expect a significant rise in bidder numbers. No state TOT projects currently up for bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Have any material orders been won this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No new orders were bagged in Q1 due to no major award activity; a few change-of-scope works worth ₹800-900 crore were secured on existing assets. Second half typically stronger for inflows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on TOT-20, TOT-21 and TOT-22 and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: NHAI raised initial capex, which the TOT operator must fund from day 1 along with an upfront payment; bidding postponed to late August. Management says the change applies to all bidders and does not hinder its bid, with the final decision depending on viability and MLFF clarifications.

qa_highlights.question: Is NHAI award pace changing for HAM, EPC and BOT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focused on TOT and select viable BOT projects, does not track HAM/EPC daily, and acknowledged the award pace was slow in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is toll growth sustainable at 15-20% compounding?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs rose ~3-3.5% last year and ~2.5% from April 1, 2026; with inflation at 6-7%, higher tariff growth is expected next year. Traffic remains robust and geopolitical tensions have had no meaningful impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will construction and O&M revenue mix shift, and what O&M orders to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction revenue is falling as active EPC projects complete; O&M share rising QoQ. Expect O&M order book to grow ₹4,000-5,000 crore annually depending on TOT wins. BOT and InvIT EBITDA margins expected to hold at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will BOT competition ease after the net-worth criteria change, and are state TOT projects coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Healthy competition expected to continue for viable BOT projects; some projects drew no bids on viability grounds. No state TOT projects are currently up for bidding.

risks_watch: Slow NHAI award cadence: no orders won in Q1; order inflow depends on second-half awards and the late-August TOT bid timing.
Higher upfront capex and MLFF clarifications for TOT-20/21/22 could affect bid economics.
Construction revenue decline (-21% YoY) continues as EPC projects complete; monitor the ₹40-43 billion two-year conversion.
Finance cost includes a one-time ₹37 crore charge; underlying interest saving is ~₹61 crore YoY.
BOT margins depend on timing of major maintenance; a maintenance-heavy year could lower the 90-91% margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating and InvIT trends, with clear targets such as net debt-free by FY2030. Cautious and somewhat evasive on order inflow, which was nil in Q1, and on TOT-20/21/22 bid economics, which the company said it would assess later.
key_quotes: Going forward, depending on the number of TOT projects we win, we expect the O&M order book to increase by around ₹4,000–₹5,000 crore every year.
As we bag more TOT projects, the order acquisition will primarily be in the O&M segment.
We expect the revenue mix to become more balanced, with O&M contributing around 40–50% of our total segment revenue alongside construction, moving towards an approximately 50:50 mix.

growth.why: Consolidated income was flat (+0.4% YoY) with construction down 21%, and no major orders won in Q1; the ₹40–43bn construction revenue over two years is backed by the existing order book, but no new capacity is being added and TOT bidding has slipped to late August.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA up 17% to ₹1,188 crore; InvIT margin at 94% (90-94% range) and BOT margin at 90-91%, with management expecting these margins to hold, while construction (lower-margin) share falls and O&M share rises.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new physical capacity is planned, but the TOT-20/21/22 bid (late August 2026) and the binding term sheet for a ₹4,605 crore asset transfer to the private InvIT could add toll and O&M capacity if won or completed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Average daily toll across subsidiaries plus both InvITs is ~₹27 crore vs ₹21.4 crore (+26% YoY), and traffic is described as robust; however, construction income fell 21% and no orders were won in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is focused on TOT and viable BOT projects; the TOT-20/21/22 bid is due late August with higher upfront capex, and the pipeline is ~₹4.4 lakh crore, but no state TOT projects are up for bidding now and the award pace is slow.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Tariffs are expected to rise in FY28 given 6-7% inflation (FY27 tariff rise was ~2.5%), and second-half inflows are expected to be stronger, but Q1 order inflow was nil.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Construction income fell 21% YoY to ₹967 crore as EPC projects complete, Q1 orders were nil, and TOT-20/21/22 bid economics may worsen with higher upfront capex and MLFF uncertainty.

rows.label: Second-half order inflows and TOT awards
rows.why: Order book is ~₹44,100 crore with no major Q1 wins; management expects stronger H2 inflows and TOT awards of ₹40,000-50,000 crore annually, with O&M order book adding ₹4,000-5,000 crore per year, but the TOT-20/21/22 bid is postponed to late August.

rows.label: Refinancing savings and net debt-free by FY2030
rows.why: Refinancing of ~₹11,000 crore across six Private InvIT SPVs cuts borrowing cost ~160 bps (~₹180 crore annual saving) and ~₹3,700 crore Mumbai-Pune debt cuts ~65 bps (~₹25 crore); net debt-free by FY2030 is retained.

rows.label: FY28 tariff revisions on inflation
rows.why: FY27 tariff increase was about 2.5%, while inflation is 6-7%, so management expects higher tariff revisions in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on InvIT toll growth, refinancing savings and the FY2030 net debt-free target, but cautious and somewhat evasive on nil Q1 order inflow and TOT-20/21/22 bid economics; analysts probed order flow and the toll-growth sustainability.

oneOffs.what: ₹37 crore one-time charge within finance cost in Q1 FY27 (underlying finance cost ₹401 crore), which depresses PAT growth
Private InvIT YoY comparison is like-for-like excluding 3 transferred assets; reported InvIT income +87% includes asset transfers into the InvIT structure
